hook: NASA crashed a full-size air taxi with test dummies strapped inside.
narration: NASA dropped a full-size air taxi onto the ground, with crash test dummies strapped inside.
This was NASA's Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia.
It was an electric air taxi design that lifts straight up.
A giant steel gantry lifts the craft on cables, then lets go, so engineers control exactly how it hits.
Cameras all around the pad caught the impact from every side.
The hit split the shell open.
Air taxis are meant to carry people over cities, so NASA wants to know how they hold up in a crash.
outcome: The air taxi ended up a crumpled wreck, with its test dummies still strapped in their seats.
title: Air taxi crash test with dummies inside
question_comment: Would you ride in an air taxi over a city?

facts.claim: Full-scale crash test of an eVTOL concept vehicle at Langley's LandIR facility in Hampton, Virginia
facts.source_quote: NASA researchers recently completed a full-scale crash test of an electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) concept vehicle at the Landing and Impact Research (LandIR) facility at NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia.

facts.claim: Air mobility aircraft move people and cargo
facts.source_quote: NASA’s vision for AAM is to help emerging aviation markets safely develop an air transportation system that moves people and cargo between places previously not served or underserved by aviation.

facts.claim: Purpose is to learn how they act in a crash
facts.source_quote: Understanding how these future aircraft may act in a crash scenario is another key point of research.

description:
NASA crash tested a full-scale electric air taxi concept, with test dummies aboard, at the Landing and Impact Research facility at Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, in 2022. No one was aboard.
